methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: WorkAI Lab at Roanoke College represents institutional capacity-building outside major metros, creating peer learning infrastructure that could distribute deep AI fluency beyond NoVA's gravitational pull—a critical test of whether educational institutions can decentralize expertise.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - wtkr.com
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly target the distribution challenge through grassroots knowledge transfer, signaling potential for peer-to-peer learning networks that could prevent Hampton Roads from falling into the widening gap scenario.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's policy incoherence—promoting AI while cooling on data centers—reveals concentration of both infrastructure and policy expertise in NoVA, while lacking distributed governance capacity to balance statewide interests versus localized economic development.

signals.title: Google to invest millions for Virginia workforce development amid data center growth - WRIC ABC 8News
signals.signal_reading: Google's workforce investment tied to data center growth suggests platform-mediated training rather than deep skill-building—concentrating shallow AI adoption around infrastructure hubs without necessarily building distributed technical depth or agency.

signals.title: Appalachian Power sees ‘explosive’ growth from data centers, other big customers
signals.signal_reading: Appalachian Power's data center growth in underserved regions creates infrastructure extraction without capability distribution—power flows out while AI expertise and economic benefit concentrate elsewhere, risking colonial development patterns that deepen rather than bridge rural-metro divides.
